essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: First major application: connecting shadow statements to Byron Katie's 'turnaround' technique for therapeutic insight
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
you can kinda tell when almost everything a person says is an attempt to fight against much larger shadow statements that are what they (or at least a part of them) actually believe. this is probably why byron katie's "turnaround" thing works

https://t.co/drWBLs9EaO https://t.co/UHEbo10E6p
Images:
- [Image #0] The image is a screenshot of a webpage that explains the concept of "turnarounds" in the context of Byron Katie's self-inquiry method, known as "The Work." The page is divided into two sections.

**Left Section:**

* The title "Turn It Around" is displayed at the top.
* A subheading reads, "Turn the thought around. Is the opposite as true as or truer than the original thought?"
* A paragraph explains the process of finding opposites of an original statement on a worksheet, which can be turned around to the self, to the other, and to the opposite.
* The text notes that not every statement has three turnarounds, and some may have just one or two, or more than three.

**Right Section:**

* The title "The Turnarounds" is displayed at the top, with a subheading "Finding Opposites."
* An example is provided, where the original thought "Paul doesn't listen to me" is turned around to:
+ "I don't listen to myself."
+ "I don't listen to Paul."
+ "Paul does listen to me."

The image effectively illustrates the concept of turnarounds and how they can be applied to challenge and reframe negative thoughts.
